The Nigeria Police Force says a 16-year-old girl, who was arrested in Lagos State over the sale of her newborn for N2m, has allegedly blamed her action on financial hardship. The Force Public Relations Officer, Ani Iniedu, disclosed this in a police operational success released over the weekend and sighted by PUNCH Metro on Sunday. Iniedu stated that the police also rescued the newborn girl after detectives arrested the alleged buyers, Favour Ipoko and her husband, Isaac Ipoko. The FPRO noted that the investigation began after a complainant reported that her tenant, Favour, had told her not to be alarmed if she heard a baby crying, despite not having been pregnant. He noted that following the complaint, detectives visited the scene, where they arrested Favour and her husband and recovered the day-old baby. Make PUNCH part of your everyday experience. According to Iniedu, the teenager allegedly admitted selling the baby for N2m, citing a “financial burden” as the reason. He wrote, “A complainant reported that her tenant, Favour Ipoko (47), informed her not to be alarmed if she heard a baby crying, despite not having been pregnant. He concluded that the case had been transferred to the State Criminal Investigation Department, Panti, Lagos, for further investigation. PUNCH Metro reported on April 18 that operatives of the Nigeria Security and Civil Defence Corps, Lagos State Command, busted a baby factory in Okuju, Ilado, Badagry area of Lagos. The operatives had rescued 18 pregnant women and 10 children, and arrested the operators of the facility, Joy Okeke and Raphael Agwu, during the operation. The victims were said to have subscribed to the facility via an offer on a Facebook platform. The pregnant women, upon delivery, have their children sold and are paid between N500,000 and N1.8m.
